label: prop:Ht_SDS
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:Ht_SDS}
For any $\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$ and $t\in{\mathbbm R}$, the following hold:
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item If $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$, then the pressure of $H(\Psi|\Phi,t)$
exists and coincides with the pressure of $\Psi$.
\item If either $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}^{\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits^{\gamma}\!\!\!\!}$ for some $\gamma>2d$ and
$\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{s}$, or $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}^{\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits^{\gamma}\!\!\!\!}$ for some $\gamma>d$ and
$\Psi\in\leftindex_1{\mathcal B}$, then the specific energy  of
$H(\Psi|\Phi,t)$ exists and is given by
$$
E_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)}=\tau_\Phi^{-t}(E(\Psi)).
$$
\item If the local Hamiltonian families $H(\Phi)$ and $H(\Psi)$ generate
dynamics $\tau_\Phi$ and $\tau_\Psi$, then $H(\Psi|\Phi,t)$ generates the
dynamics
$$
\alpha_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)}^s=\tau^{-t}_\Phi\circ\tau^s_\Psi\circ\tau^t_\Phi,
$$
for $s,t\in{\mathbbm R}$.
\end{romanenumerate}
head: environment

label: thm:entropy_energy_cons
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:entropy_energy_cons}
Let $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}^{\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits^{\gamma}\!\!\!\!}$, $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$, and $t\in{\mathbbm R}$.
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item If $\gamma>2d$, then
$$
s(\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t)=s(\omega).
$$
\item If $\gamma>d$, then
$$
(\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t)(E(\Phi))=\omega(E(\Phi)).
$$
\end{romanenumerate}
head: environment

label: thm:W_disapp
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:W_disapp}
Let $\Psi\in\leftindex_1{\mathcal B}$ and $t\in{\mathbbm R}$.
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item If $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}^{\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits^{\gamma}\!\!\!\!}$ with $\gamma>d$, then
$$
\lim_\Lambda\frac1{|\Lambda|}
\left\|\tau_\Phi^{-t}(H_\Lambda(\Psi))-H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)\right\|
=0.
$$
\item If $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}^{\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits^{\gamma}\!\!\!\!}$ with $\gamma>2d$, then the
surface energy $W(\Psi|\Phi,t)$ of $H(\Psi|\Phi,t)$ exists and satisfies
$$
\lim_\Lambda\frac1{|\Lambda|}\|W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)\|=0.
$$
\end{romanenumerate}
In particular, under the assumptions of Part~\textup{(ii)}, if in addition
$\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$, then the pair
$(\Phi,\Psi)$ satisfies~\cite[Condition~\textbf{(SD)}]{Jaksic2026a}.
head: environment

label: prop:state_properties
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{(i)} Since $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$, one has
$s(\omega)=\omega(E(\Psi))+P(\Psi)$.
By Theorem~\ref{thm:entropy_energy_cons} and Proposition~\ref{prop:Ht_SDS}, we further
have $s(\omega)=s(\omega_t)$, $P_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)}=P(\Psi)$ and
$E_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)}=\tau^{-t}_\Phi(E(\Psi))$.
Hence, 
\[s(\omega_t)=\omega_t(E_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)})+P_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)},\]
 and so
$\omega_t\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(H(\Psi|\Phi,t))$.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(ii)}
Since $\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$ and $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$,
$\omega$ is an $(\tau_\Psi,1)$-KMS state
by~\cite[Theorems~A and~B]{Araki2003}.
For $A,B\in{\mathfrak A}$, set $A_t=\tau_\Phi^t(A)$ and $B_t=\tau_\Phi^t(B)$.
Proposition~\ref{prop:Ht_SDS}\textup{(iii)} gives
$$
\omega_t(A\alpha_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)}^s(B))
=
\omega(A_t\tau_\Psi^s(B_t)),
$$
so $\omega_t$ is an $(\alpha_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)},1)$-KMS state.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(iii)}
Since the surface energies $W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)$ are well-defined for
every $\Lambda$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:formula_W}),
\cite[Pro\-position~6.2.17]{Bratteli1981} implies that the
$(\alpha_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)},1)$-KMS state $\omega_t$ satisfies the Gibbs
condition with respect to $H(\Psi|\Phi,t)$.
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: prop:core
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{prop:core}
Suppose that $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}^{\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits^{\gamma}\!\!\!\!}$ with $\gamma>2d$ and
$\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$. For $t\in{\mathbbm R}$, let $\delta_t$ be the $\ast$-derivation
generating the dynamics
$$
\alpha_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)}^s
=\tau_\Phi^{-t}\circ\tau_\Psi^s\circ\tau_\Phi^t.
$$
Then ${{\mathfrak{A}}_{\mathrm{loc}}}$ is a core for $\delta_t$ for every $t\in{\mathbbm R}$.

label: thm:comot
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:comot}
Let $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}^{\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits^{\gamma}\!\!\!\!}$ with $\gamma>2d$ and
$\Psi\in\leftindex_1{\mathcal B}\cap{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$. Then $\Psi$ is
$\tau_\Phi$-invariant iff
$\tau_\Phi^t\circ\tau_\Psi^s=\tau_\Psi^s\circ\tau_\Phi^t$
for all $s,t\in{\mathbbm R}$.

label: thm:wgPreserv
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
In case~\textup{(ii)}, the proof gives a stronger conclusion than
weak Gibbsianity: for every $t\in{\mathbbm R}$ there exists a constant $C_t\geq1$, independent of the finite interval
$\Lambda\subset{\mathbbm Z}$, such that
$$
C_t^{-1}\omega_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t),\Lambda}
\leq
(\omega_t)_\Lambda
\leq
C_t\omega_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t),\Lambda},
$$
where
$$
\omega_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t),\Lambda}
=
\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)}}
{\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits(\mathrm{e}^{-H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)})}.
$$
This follows from~\eqref{eq:boundsThm31} and the uniform bounds of
Theorem~\ref{thm:d1_extension}. In particular, for every $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$,
$$
\left|
S(\nu_\Lambda|(\omega_t)_\Lambda)
-
S(\nu_\Lambda|\omega_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t),\Lambda})
\right|
\leq
\log C_t.
$$
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
Assume that $(\omega,\Psi)$ is a regular pair and that either
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item $\|\Psi\|_r<r$ for some $r>0$, or
\item $d=1$ and $\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$.
\end{romanenumerate}
Let $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$ and consider $\omega_t=\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t$ for
$t\in{\mathbbm R}$. Then there exists $T>0$ such that, for every $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ and
every $|t|<T$, the specific relative entropy $s(\nu_t|\omega_t)$, where
$\nu_t=\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^t$, exists and satisfies
$$
s(\nu_t|\omega_t)=s(\nu|\omega).
$$
In particular, $(\omega_t,H(\Psi|\Phi,t))$ is a regular pair for every
$|t|<T$. One can take $T=\infty$ in case~\textup{(ii)} or if $\omega$ is
$\tau_\Phi$-invariant.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $(\omega,\Psi)$ is a regular pair, $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$.
Under either assumption~\textup{(i)} or~\textup{(ii)},
\cite[Theorem~2.11]{Jaksic2023a} gives
${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)={\mathcal S}_\mathrm{wg}(\Psi)$, and hence $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{wg}(\Psi)$.
With $T$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:wgPreserv}, we have
$\omega_t\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{wg}(H(\Psi|\Phi,t))$ for $|t|<T$, and one can take
$T=\infty$ in case~\textup{(ii)}. Since $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$, the conservation
of specific entropy gives
$s(\nu_t)=s(\nu)$, while Proposition~\ref{prop:Ht_SDS} gives
$P_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)}=P(\Psi)$ and
$\nu_t(E_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)})=\nu(E(\Psi))$. Since $\omega_t\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{wg}(H(\Psi|\Phi,t))$, the argument
of~\cite[Proposition~2.10]{Jaksic2023a}, applied to the family
$H(\Psi|\Phi,t)$, gives
\[
\begin{split}
s(\nu_t|\omega_t)
&=-s(\nu_t)+\nu_t(E_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)})+P_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)}\\
&=-s(\nu)+\nu(E(\Psi))+P(\Psi)\\
&=s(\nu|\omega),
                
\end{split}
\]
for $|t|<T$, and for all $t\in{\mathbbm R}$ in case~\textup{(ii)}.

Suppose now that $\omega$ is $\tau_\Phi$-invariant. Fix $t\in{\mathbbm R}$,
choose an integer $n\geq1$ such that $|t|/n<T$, and set $h=t/n$.
Since $\omega_h=\omega$, 
$s(\nu_{(k+1)h}|\omega)=s(\nu_{kh}|\omega)$ for
$k=0,\ldots,n-1$, and hence
$$
s(\nu_t|\omega)=s(\nu|\omega).
$$
Finally, for any $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$, regularity of $(\omega,\Psi)$ applied
to $\nu_{-t}$, together with the last identity, the conservation of
specific entropy, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:Ht_SDS}, gives
\[
\begin{split}
s(\nu|\omega)
&=s(\nu_{-t}|\omega)
=-s(\nu_{-t})+\nu_{-t}(E(\Psi))+P(\Psi)\\
&=-s(\nu)+\nu(E_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)})+P_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)}.
\end{split}
\]
Thus $(\omega,H(\Psi|\Phi,t))$ is regular for every $t\in{\mathbbm R}$.
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: lem:Hiai
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Hiai}
Let $t\in{\mathbbm R}$. If $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ satisfies the Gibbs condition for
$H(\Psi|\Phi,t)$, then
$$
S(\rho_\Lambda|\omega_\Lambda)
\leq
S(\rho_\Lambda|\omega_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t),\Lambda})
+2\|W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)\|
$$
for any $\rho\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ and $\Lambda\in{\mathcal F}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We follow~\cite[Lemma~2.3]{Hiai1993a}. $S(\,{\bm\cdot}\,|\,{\bm\cdot}\,)$ denotes Araki's relative entropy. 
 By assumption,
$$
\omega_{-W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)}
=
\omega_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t),\Lambda}\otimes\nu
$$
for some state $\nu$ on ${\mathfrak A}_{\Lambda^c}$. Monotonicity under restriction
and the perturbation bound~\cite[Eq.~(2.3)]{Hiai1993a} give
\begin{align*}
S(\rho_\Lambda|\omega_\Lambda)
&\leq S(\rho_\Lambda\otimes\nu|\omega)\\
&\leq S(\rho_\Lambda\otimes\nu|
\omega_{-W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)})
+2\|W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)\|\\
&=S(\rho_\Lambda\otimes\nu|
\omega_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t),\Lambda}\otimes\nu)
+2\|W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)\|\\
&=S(\rho_\Lambda|\omega_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t),\Lambda})
+2\|W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)\|,
\end{align*}
as claimed.
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: prop:gibbs
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:gibbs}
Let $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}^{\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits^{\gamma}\!\!\!\!}$ with $\gamma>2d$ and
$\Psi\in\leftindex_1{\mathcal B}\cap{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$.
For $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ and $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$, set
$\nu_t=\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^t$ and $\omega_t=\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t$.
Then, for every $t\in{\mathbbm R}$,
$$
\limsup_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}
S((\nu_t)_\Lambda|(\omega_t)_\Lambda)
\leq
-s(\nu)+\nu(E(\Psi))+P(\Psi).
$$
In particular, if $(\omega,\Psi)$ is a regular pair, the right-hand
side equals $s(\nu|\omega)$, and
$$
s(\nu_t|\omega_t)\leq s(\nu|\omega)
$$
whenever $s(\nu_t|\omega_t)$ exists.
head: environment

label: eq:limsup_bound
title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:state_properties}, $\omega_t$ satisfies
the Gibbs condition for $H(\Psi|\Phi,t)$. Since
Theorem~\ref{thm:W_disapp} gives
$\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}|\Lambda|^{-1}\|W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)\|=0$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:Hiai} yields
\begin{align*}
\limsup_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}
S((\nu_t)_\Lambda|(\omega_t)_\Lambda)
&\leq
\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}
S((\nu_t)_\Lambda|\omega_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t),\Lambda})
+2\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}\|W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)\|\\[2pt]
&=
\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}
\left(
-S((\nu_t)_\Lambda)
+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits((\nu_t)_\Lambda H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t))
+\log\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits\mathrm{e}^{-H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)}
\right)\\[2pt]
&=
-s(\nu_t)
+\nu_t(E_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)})
+P_{H(\Psi|\Phi,t)}.
\end{align*}
Theorem~\ref{thm:entropy_energy_cons} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:Ht_SDS} give
\begin{equation}
\limsup_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}
S((\nu_t)_\Lambda|(\omega_t)_\Lambda)
\leq
-s(\nu)+\nu(E(\Psi))+P(\Psi),
\label{eq:limsup_bound}
\end{equation}
as claimed. If $(\omega,\Psi)$ is regular, the right-hand side
of~\eqref{eq:limsup_bound} equals $s(\nu|\omega)$.
If $s(\nu_t|\omega_t)$ exists, it equals the limsup on the left.
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

title: Corollary
body_md:
Under the assumptions of Proposition~\ref{prop:gibbs}, suppose that
$(\omega,\Psi)$ is a regular pair and that $\omega$ is
$\tau_\Phi$-invariant. Then, for every $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ and $t\in{\mathbbm R}$,
$$
s(\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^t|\omega)=s(\nu|\omega).
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Regularity of $(\omega,\Psi)$ implies that both relative entropies exist.
Applying Proposition~\ref{prop:gibbs} at time $t$ gives
$$
s(\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^t|\omega)\leq s(\nu|\omega).
$$
Applying the same proposition at time $-t$ to
$\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^t$ gives the reverse inequality.
\hfill$\Box$

label: prop:LRboxes
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the discussion above, $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_{F_g}$ with $F_g$ given by~\eqref{eq:Fg}. 
For $t\in{\mathbbm R}$ and $\Lambda'\subset\Lambda\subset\widetilde\Lambda\in{\mathcal F}$,
\cite[Theorem~3.4(ii)]{Nachtergaele2019} gives
$$
\left\|\tau_{\Phi,\Lambda}^t(A)
-\tau^t_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}(A)\right\|
\leq
\dfrac{2{\|A\|}}{C_{F_g}}
\mathrm{e}^{2I_t(\Phi)}I_t(\Phi)
\sum_{(x,y)\in\Lambda'\times(\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda)}
F_g(|x-y|),
$$
where $I_t(\Phi)\coloneq C_{F_g}{\|\Phi\|}_{F_g}|t|$. 
Using~\eqref{eq:bound_double_sum}, we obtain
$$
\left\|\tau_{\Phi,\Lambda}^t(A)
-\tau^t_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}(A)\right\|
\leq
2{\|A\|}{\|\Phi\|}_{F_g}|t|
\mathrm{e}^{2C_{F_g}{\|\Phi\|}_{F_g}|t|}
\VERT F\VERT|\Lambda'|
\mathrm{e}^{-g(\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(\Lambda',\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda))}.
$$
This inequality and the bounds $C_{F_g}\leq C_F\leq2^\gamma\VERT F\VERT$ and
$\|\Phi\|_{F_g}\leq\|\Phi\|_{\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits^\gamma}$ yield~\eqref{mar-don} with
$$
c_{\Phi,\delta,t}
=
2\|\Phi\|_{\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits^\gamma}\VERT F\VERT |t|\,
\mathrm{e}^{2^{1+\gamma}\|\Phi\|_{\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits^\gamma}\VERT F\VERT |t|}.
$$
\hfill$\Box$

label: lem:boxes
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:boxes} Fix $\gamma>2d$ and $d<\delta<\gamma-d$. Let $\{\Lambda\}$ be an
increasing family of cubes centered at the origin that exhausts ${\mathbbm Z}^d$.
Then there exist concentric subcubes $\Lambda'\subset\Lambda$
 such that
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item $\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac{|\Lambda'|}{|\Lambda|}=1$.
\item $\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}|\Lambda'|
\left(1+\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(\Lambda',\Lambda^c)\right)^{-\delta}=0$.
\end{romanenumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write the cubes of the family as $\Lambda=\Lambda_L\coloneq\llbracket-L,L\rrbracket^d$ 
where $L\to\infty$. Choose $0<p<1-d/\delta$, set $r_L\coloneq\lfloor L^{1-p}\rfloor$, 
and define
$$
\Lambda'=\Lambda_L'
\coloneq
\llbracket-L+r_L,L-r_L\rrbracket^d.
$$

\textbf{(i)}
Since $r_L/L\to0$, we have
$$
\frac{|\Lambda_L'|}{|\Lambda_L|}
=
\left(
\frac{2(L-r_L)+1}{2L+1}
\right)^d
\rightarrow1.
$$

\noindent\textbf{(ii)}
Since
$$
\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(\Lambda_L',\Lambda_L^c)=r_L+1,
$$
we have, for some constant $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $L$,
$$
|\Lambda_L'|
\left(1+\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(\Lambda_L',\Lambda_L^c)\right)^{-\delta}
\leq
cL^{d-(1-p)\delta}.
$$
The exponent $d-(1-p)\delta$ is negative, so the right-hand side
tends to zero.
\hfill$\Box$

label: prop:energy_loc_glob
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:energy_loc_glob}
Let $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}^{\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits^{\gamma}\!\!\!\!}$ and assume either
$\gamma>2d$ and $\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{s}$, or
$\gamma>d$ and $\Psi\in\leftindex_1{\mathcal B}$.
Let $\{\Lambda\}$ be an increasing family of cubes centered at the origin
that exhausts ${\mathbbm Z}^d$. Then, for any $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ and $t$,
$$
\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}
\left|\left(\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t-\omega\circ\tau^t_{\Phi,\Lambda}\right)
(H_\Lambda(\Psi))\right|
=
\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}
\left\|\left(\tau^t_\Phi-\tau^t_{\Phi,\Lambda}\right)
(H_\Lambda(\Psi))\right\|
=0.
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since
$$
\left|\left(\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t-\omega\circ\tau^t_{\Phi,\Lambda}\right)
(H_\Lambda(\Psi))\right|
\leq
\left\|\left(\tau^t_\Phi-\tau^t_{\Phi,\Lambda}\right)
(H_\Lambda(\Psi))\right\|,
$$
it suffices to prove that the second limit is zero.

Suppose first that $\gamma>d$ and $\Psi\in\leftindex_1{\mathcal B}$. Fix
$0<\delta<\gamma-d$. Theorem~\ref{thm:bound_Lieb_Rob} gives
\begin{align*}
\left\|\left(\tau^t_\Phi-\tau^t_{\Phi,\Lambda}\right)
(H_\Lambda(\Psi))\right\|
&\leq
c_{\Phi,\delta,t}
\sum_{X\subset\Lambda}
\frac{|X|}{\left(1+\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(X,\Lambda^c)\right)^\delta}
\|\Psi(X)\|\\
&\leq
c_{\Phi,\delta,t}\leftindex_1\|\Psi\|
\sum_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac1{\left(1+\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(x,\Lambda^c)\right)^\delta}.
\end{align*}
For $r\in{\mathbbm N}$, set
\begin{equation}
\partial_r\Lambda
\coloneq
\left\{x\in\Lambda\mid\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(x,\Lambda^c)\leq r\right\}.
\label{eq:deltarDef}
\end{equation}
Then
$$
\frac1{|\Lambda|}
\sum_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac1{\left(1+\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(x,\Lambda^c)\right)^\delta}
\leq
\frac{|\partial_r\Lambda|}{|\Lambda|}
+
\frac1{(1+r)^\delta}.
$$
Taking the limit along the cubes and then letting $r\to\infty$ proves the
claim in this case.

It remains to consider $\gamma>2d$ and $\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{s}$.
Fix $d<\delta<\gamma-d$ and choose the subcubes $\Lambda'$
provided by Lemma~\ref{lem:boxes}.  We claim
that, for some constants $c_1,c_2$,
\begin{equation}
\left\|\left(\tau^t_\Phi-\tau^t_{\Phi,\Lambda}\right)(H_\Lambda(\Psi))\right\|
\leq
c_1|\Lambda'|^2
\left(1+\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(\Lambda',\Lambda^c)\right)^{-\delta}
+c_2|\Lambda\setminus\Lambda'|.
\label{eq:ineq1}
\end{equation}
The result  then follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:boxes}, as in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:entropy}.

Set
$$
\tilde H_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(\Psi)
\coloneq
H_\Lambda(\Psi)-H_{\Lambda'}(\Psi).
$$
Invoking Theorem~\ref{thm:bound_Lieb_Rob}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
\left\|\left(\tau^t_\Phi-\tau^t_{\Phi,\Lambda}\right)(H_\Lambda(\Psi))\right\|
&\leq
\left\|\left(\tau^t_\Phi-\tau^t_{\Phi,\Lambda}\right)
(H_{\Lambda'}(\Psi))\right\|
+
\left\|\tau^t_\Phi(\tilde H_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(\Psi))\right\|
+
\left\|\tau^t_{\Phi,\Lambda}(\tilde H_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(\Psi))\right\|\\[4pt]
&\leq
c_{\Phi,\delta,t}\|H_{\Lambda'}(\Psi)\||\Lambda'|
\left(1+\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(\Lambda',\Lambda^c)\right)^{-\delta}
+2\|\tilde H_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(\Psi)\|.
\end{align*}
We also have 
$$
\|H_{\Lambda'}(\Psi)\|
\leq
\sum_{X\cap\Lambda'\neq\emptyset}\|\Psi(X)\|
\leq
|\Lambda'|\sum_{X\ni0}\|\Psi(X)\|
\leq
|\Lambda'|\|\Psi\|_\mathrm{s},
$$
and similarly,
$$
\|\tilde H_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(\Psi)\|
\leq
\sum_{X\cap(\Lambda\setminus\Lambda')\neq\emptyset}\|\Psi(X)\|
\leq
|\Lambda\setminus\Lambda'|\|\Psi\|_\mathrm{s}.
$$
Thus~\eqref{eq:ineq1} holds with
$c_1=c_{\Phi,\delta,t}\|\Psi\|_\mathrm{s}$ and
$c_2=2\|\Psi\|_\mathrm{s}$.
\hfill$\Box$

label: prop:formula_W
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: eq:est_surface_en0
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $d<\delta<\gamma-d$, $\Lambda\in{\mathcal F}$, and let
$\widetilde\Lambda$ run through the finite supersets of $\Lambda$, directed
by inclusion. By definition,
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
W_{\Lambda,\widetilde\Lambda}(\Psi|\Phi,t)
&=
H_{\widetilde\Lambda}(\Psi|\Phi,t)
-
H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)
-
H_{\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda}(\Psi|\Phi,t)
\\[8pt]
&=
\sum_{X\subset\widetilde\Lambda}
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}\left(\Psi(X)\right)
-
\sum_{X\subset\Lambda}
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\Lambda}\left(\Psi(X)\right)
-
\sum_{X\subset\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda}
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda}
\left(\Psi(X)\right)
\\[8pt]
&=
\sum_{X\subset\Lambda}
\left(
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}
-
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\Lambda}
\right)(\Psi(X))
+
\sum_{X\subset\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda}
\left(
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}
-
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda}
\right)(\Psi(X))
\\
&\qquad
+
\sum_{\mathclap{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{1}{X\subset\widetilde\Lambda}{X\cap\Lambda\neq\emptyset\neq
X\cap(\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda)}}}
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}(\Psi(X))
\\[4pt]
&=
\left(
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}
-
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\Lambda}
\right)(H_\Lambda(\Psi))
+
\left(
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}
-
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda}
\right)
(H_{\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda}(\Psi))
\\
&\qquad
+
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}
\left(W_{\Lambda,\widetilde\Lambda}(\Psi)\right).
\end{split}
\label{eq:est_surface_en0}
\end{equation}
Since $H_\Lambda(\Psi)\in{\mathfrak A}_\Lambda$ is fixed, the first term
after the last equality sign in~\eqref{eq:est_surface_en0} converges to
$$
\left(
\tau^{-t}_\Phi-\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\Lambda}
\right)(H_\Lambda(\Psi)),
$$
which is the first term on the right-hand side
of~\eqref{eq:surf_energy_formula}. To deal with the second term, for $X\subset\Lambda^c$ set
$$
D_{\widetilde\Lambda}(X)
\coloneq
\begin{cases}
\left(
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}
-
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda}
\right)(\Psi(X))
&\text{if }X\subset\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda;\\[4pt]
0&\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
$$
Since $H_{\widetilde\Lambda}(\Phi|_{\Lambda^c})
=H_{\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda}(\Phi)$,
norm convergence of the finite-volume dynamics for $\Phi$ and
$\Phi|_{\Lambda^c}$ along the inclusion-directed net gives,
for every $X\subset\Lambda^c$,
$$
\lim_{\widetilde\Lambda}D_{\widetilde\Lambda}(X)
=
\left(
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi}
-
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi|_{\Lambda^c}}
\right)(\Psi(X)).
$$
By Proposition~\ref{prop:LRboxes}, there exists a constant
$c_{\Phi,\delta,t}$ such that
\begin{equation}
\|D_{\widetilde\Lambda}(X)\|
\leq
c_{\Phi,\delta,t}
\frac{|X|}
{\left(1+\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(X,\Lambda)\right)^\delta}
\|\Psi(X)\|.
\label{eq:est_surface_en1}
\end{equation}
The right-hand side is summable over $X\subset\Lambda^c$
by~\eqref{eq:est_surface_en2}. Therefore, by dominated convergence,
\[
\lim_{\widetilde\Lambda}
\left(
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}
-
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda}
\right)
(H_{\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda}(\Psi))
=
\lim_{\widetilde\Lambda}
\sum_{X\subset\Lambda^c}D_{\widetilde\Lambda}(X)
=
\sum_{X\subset\Lambda^c}
\left(
\tau^{-t}_\Phi
-
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi|_{\Lambda^c}}
\right)(\Psi(X)).
\]
Finally we  consider
$\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}
(W_{\Lambda,\widetilde\Lambda}(\Psi))$. Since
$\Psi\in\leftindex_1{\mathcal B}\subset{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{s}$, the series defining
$W_\Lambda(\Psi)$ is absolutely convergent, and so
$$
\lim_{\widetilde\Lambda}
\left\|
W_{\Lambda,\widetilde\Lambda}(\Psi)-W_\Lambda(\Psi)
\right\|
=0.
$$
Moreover,
\[
\left\|
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}
\left(W_{\Lambda,\widetilde\Lambda}(\Psi)\right)
-
\tau^{-t}_\Phi\left(W_\Lambda(\Psi)\right)
\right\|
\leq
\left\|
W_{\Lambda,\widetilde\Lambda}(\Psi)-W_\Lambda(\Psi)
\right\|
+
\left\|
\left(
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}
-
\tau^{-t}_\Phi
\right)
\left(W_\Lambda(\Psi)\right)
\right\|.
\]
The first term tends to zero by absolute convergence of the series
defining $W_\Lambda(\Psi)$. The second tends to zero because
$\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}(W_\Lambda(\Psi))$
converges in norm to $\tau^{-t}_\Phi(W_\Lambda(\Psi))$
as $\widetilde\Lambda$ increases to ${\mathbbm Z}^d$. Thus,
$$
\lim_{\widetilde\Lambda}
\tau^{-t}_{\Phi,\widetilde\Lambda}
\left(W_{\Lambda,\widetilde\Lambda}(\Psi)\right)
=
\tau^{-t}_\Phi\left(W_\Lambda(\Psi)\right).
$$
Taking the limit in~\eqref{eq:est_surface_en0} proves
\eqref{eq:surf_energy_formula}. \hfill$\Box$

label: mar-bd
title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{(i)} Recall that  $F(u)=(1+u)^{-\gamma}$  is an $F$-function satisfying 
$\|\Phi\|_F\leq\|\Phi\|_{\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits^\gamma}$. The infinite-volume
Lieb--Robinson bound~\cite[Corollary~3.6(i)]{Nachtergaele2019} gives a
constant $L_t<\infty$, depending only on $\Phi$, $\gamma$ and $t$, such
that
\begin{equation}
\|[\tau_\Phi^t(C),D]\|
\leq L_t\|C\|\|D\|
\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{z\in Z}F(|x-z|)
\label{mar-bd}
\end{equation}
for disjoint $X,Z\in{\mathcal F}$, $C\in{\mathfrak A}_X$ and $D\in{\mathfrak A}_Z$. Increasing $L_t$
to at least $2$ extends this bound to intersecting supports, since
$F(0)=1$ and $\|[\tau_\Phi^t(C),D]\|\leq2\|C\|\|D\|$.
Fix $A\in{\mathfrak A}_\Lambda$. Since $\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}\subset{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{s}$, translation
invariance gives
$\sum_{Z\ni z}\|\Psi(Z)\|=\|\Psi\|_{\mathrm s}$ for every $z\in{\mathbbm Z}^d$.
Summing  bound~\eqref{mar-bd} with $C=A$ and $D=\Psi(Z)$, we obtain
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
	\sum_{Z\in{\mathcal F}}\|[\Psi(Z),\tau_\Phi^t(A)]\|
	&\leq L_t\|A\|
	\sum_{x\in\Lambda}\sum_{z\in{\mathbbm Z}^d}
	F(|x-z|)\sum_{Z\ni z}\|\Psi(Z)\|\\
	&=L_t\VERT F\VERT\|\Psi\|_{\mathrm s}|\Lambda|\|A\|.
\end{split}
\label{mar-tue}
\end{equation}
In particular,  setting $G=\tau_\Phi^t(A)$, the series
$$
S\coloneq\sum_{Z\in{\mathcal F}}\mathrm{i}[\Psi(Z),G]
$$
converges  absolutely  in norm. We proceed to show that
$G\in\mathop{\mathrm{Dom}}\nolimits(\delta_\Psi)$ and that $\delta_\Psi(G)=S$.

Let $\Gamma$ be a finite cube and 
$S_\Gamma=\mathrm{i}[H_\Gamma(\Psi),G]$. Absolute convergence implies that
$S_\Gamma$ converges in norm to $S$ as $\Gamma$ exhausts ${\mathbbm Z}^d$. Write 
\begin{equation}
\tau_{\Psi,\Gamma}^s(G)-G
=\int_0^s\tau_{\Psi,\Gamma}^u(S_\Gamma)\mathrm{d} u.
\label{mar-phy}
\end{equation}
Obviously,  
$$
\|\tau_{\Psi,\Gamma}^u(S_\Gamma)-\tau_\Psi^u(S)\|
\leq\|S_\Gamma-S\|
+\|\tau_{\Psi,\Gamma}^u(S)-\tau_\Psi^u(S)\|,
$$
and since  $\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$, the  right-hand side tends to zero uniformly for $u$ in compact intervals.
Passing to the limit in~\eqref{mar-phy}  gives
$$
\tau_\Psi^s(G)-G=\int_0^s\tau_\Psi^u(S)\mathrm{d} u.
$$
It follows that
$\lim_{s\to0}s^{-1}(\tau_\Psi^s(G)-G)=S$, and so 
$G\in\mathop{\mathrm{Dom}}\nolimits(\delta_\Psi)$ and $\delta_\Psi(G)=S$, as claimed. Hence
$A\in\mathop{\mathrm{Dom}}\nolimits(\delta_t)$ and $\delta_t(A)=\tau_\Phi^{-t}(S)$. Since $\|\delta_t(A)\|=\|S\|\leq
\sum_{Z\in{\mathcal F}}\|[\Psi(Z),\tau_\Phi^t(A)]\|$,
the estimate~\eqref{mar-tue}  gives~\eqref{eq:core_local_bound} with
$c_t=L_t\VERT F\VERT\|\Psi\|_{\mathrm s}$.


\medskip\noindent\textbf{(ii)} Assume now that
$\Psi\in\leftindex_1{\mathcal B}$ and write
$H_\Lambda(t)=H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)$,
$W_\Lambda(t)=W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)$ and
$W_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(t)=W_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(\Psi|\Phi,t)$.
For $\Lambda'\supset\Lambda$, the definition of the surface energy gives
$$
H_{\Lambda'}(t)
=H_\Lambda(t)+H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(t)
+W_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(t).
$$
$H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(t)$  commutes with $A\in{\mathfrak A}_\Lambda$ and 
Proposition~\ref{prop:formula_W} gives norm convergence of
$W_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(t)$ to $W_\Lambda(t)$. Hence
$$
\lim_{\{\Lambda'\}}\mathrm{i}[H_{\Lambda'}(t),A]
=\mathrm{i}[H_\Lambda(t)+W_\Lambda(t),A]\eqcolon D.
$$
Writing
$\alpha_{\Lambda'}^s=\tau_{\Phi,\Lambda'}^{-t}\circ
\tau_{\Psi,\Lambda'}^s\circ\tau_{\Phi,\Lambda'}^t$, we have
$$
\alpha_{\Lambda'}^s(A)-A
=\int_0^s\alpha_{\Lambda'}^u(\mathrm{i}[H_{\Lambda'}(t),A])\mathrm{d} u.
$$
Passing to the limit, 
$$
\alpha^s(A)-A=\int_0^s\alpha^u(D)\mathrm{d} u.
$$
Differentiating at $s=0$ gives  $\delta_t(A)=D$ and completes the proof of
the lemma.
\hfill$\Box$

title: Proof
body_md:
We consider $s\geq0$; the case  $s<0$ is analogous. Let $(\tau_\iota)_{\iota\in I}$ be a net of $C^\ast$-dynamics on ${\mathfrak A}$
converging to a $C^\ast$-dynamics $\tau$ in norm on each observable,
uniformly for $s$ in compact subsets of ${\mathbbm R}$.
 If $(V_\iota)_{\iota\in I}$ is a
norm-convergent net in ${\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}$ with limit $V$, then
$$
\tau_V^s(A)=\lim_\iota(\tau_\iota)_{V_\iota}^s(A),
$$
where $\tau_V$ and $(\tau_\iota)_{V_\iota}$ denote the corresponding local
perturbations. This follows from the  Dyson expansion
$$
\tau_V^s(A)=\tau^s(A)+\sum_{n\ge1}\,
\int\limits_{0\le s_1\le\cdots\le s_n\le s}
\mathrm{i}[\tau^{s_1}(V),\mathrm{i}[\tau^{s_2}(V),\cdots\mathrm{i}[\tau^{s_n}(V),\tau^s(A)]\cdots]]
\mathrm{d} s_1\mathrm{d} s_2\cdots\mathrm{d} s_n,
$$
see, e.g., \cite[Proposition~5.4.1]{Bratteli1981}. On each compact time
interval, the corresponding integrands for $(\tau_\iota)_{V_\iota}$
converge uniformly to those above. The $n$-th integrated term is bounded by
$\|A\|(2M|s|)^n/n!$, where $M$ bounds $\|V_\iota\|$ on a tail of the net.
Uniform summability therefore proves the assertion. Moreover, if
$$
\tau_\iota^s(A)=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} sH_\iota}A\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i} sH_\iota},
$$
then
$$
(\tau_\iota)_{V_\iota}^s(A)
=
\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} s(H_\iota+V_\iota)}A\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i} s(H_\iota+V_\iota)}.
$$
We fix $\Lambda\in{\mathcal F}$ and $t\in{\mathbbm R}$.
By definition~\eqref{eq:surface_en_def}, for any $A$ in ${\mathfrak A}$ we have
$$
\alpha^s(A)=\lim_{\{\Lambda'\}}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} sH_{\Lambda'}(t)}A\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i} sH_{\Lambda'}(t)}
=\lim_{\{\Lambda'\}}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} s(H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(t)+H_\Lambda(t)+W_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(t))}A
\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i} s(H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(t)+H_\Lambda(t)+W_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(t))}.
$$
The convergence is uniform for $s$ in compact subsets of ${\mathbbm R}$,
by the finite-volume representation of $\alpha$ and the corresponding
convergence for $\tau_\Phi$ and $\tau_\Psi$.
 Thus, the previous argument yields
$$
\alpha^s_{-W_{\Lambda}(t)}(A)
=\lim_{\{\Lambda'\}}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} s(H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(t)+H_\Lambda(t)+R_{\Lambda'})}A
\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i} s(H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(t)+H_\Lambda(t)+R_{\Lambda'})}
$$
where
$R_{\Lambda'}=W_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(t)-W_\Lambda(t)$ converges to zero in
norm by Proposition~\ref{prop:formula_W}. It follows  that
\[
\begin{split}
\alpha^s_{-W_{\Lambda}(t)}(A)
&=\lim_{\{\Lambda'\}}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} s(H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(t)+H_\Lambda(t))}A
\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i} s(H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(t)+H_\Lambda(t))}\\[1mm]
&=\lim_{\{\Lambda'\}}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} sH_{\Lambda^c\cap\Lambda'}(t)}\alpha_\Lambda^s(A)
\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i} sH_{\Lambda^c\cap\Lambda'}(t)}\\[1mm]
&=\alpha_{\Lambda^c}^s\circ\alpha_\Lambda^s(A).
\end{split}
\]
\hfill$\Box$

label: lem:restricted_double_ineq
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:restricted_double_ineq} Let $t\in{\mathbbm R}$ and $\Lambda\in{\mathcal F}$. Assume that there exists $a>0$
such that, for every $K\subset{\mathbbm Z}^d$ and $A\in{{\mathfrak{A}}_{\mathrm{loc}}}$, the map
$$
{\mathbbm R}\ni s\mapsto\alpha_K^s(A)
$$
has an analytic extension to the strip
$S=\{z\in{\mathbbm C}\mid|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|<a\}$.
Suppose also that there exists a non-decreasing function $\chi:{\mathcal F}\to{\mathbbm R}_+$ such that
\begin{equation}
\|\alpha^z_K(A)\|\leq\chi(K\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A)\|A\| 
\label{mar-knee}
\end{equation}
for any $K\subset{\mathbbm Z}^d$, $A\in{{\mathfrak{A}}_{\mathrm{loc}}}$ and $z\in S$. Then, for every
$A\in{{\mathfrak{A}}_{\mathrm{loc}}}$, the map
$$
{\mathbbm R}\ni s\mapsto\alpha^s_{-W_{\Lambda}(t)}(A)
$$
has an analytic extension to $S$, and for any $z\in S$ one has  
$$
\|\alpha^z_{-W_{\Lambda}(t)}(A)\|
\leq
\chi(\Lambda^c\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A)\chi(\Lambda\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A)\|A\|.
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $A\in{{\mathfrak{A}}_{\mathrm{loc}}}$ and $z\in S$, set
$$
\beta^z(A)\coloneq\alpha^z_{\Lambda^c}\circ\alpha^z_\Lambda(A).
$$
Since
$$
\alpha^z_\Lambda(A)\in{\mathfrak A}_{\Lambda\cup\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A},
$$
and ${\mathfrak A}_{\Lambda\cup\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A}$ is finite-dimensional, an expansion of
$\alpha^z_\Lambda(A)$ in a fixed basis of this algebra shows that the map $S\ni z\mapsto\beta^z(A)$ 
is analytic. By Lemma~\ref{lem:alphactor},
$$
\beta^s(A)=\alpha^s_{-W_\Lambda(t)}(A)
$$
for $s\in{\mathbbm R}$. Thus, $\beta^z(A)$ is the analytic extension of
$\alpha^s_{-W_\Lambda(t)}(A)$ to $S$, and
$$
\alpha^z_{-W_\Lambda(t)}(A)
=
\alpha^z_{\Lambda^c}\circ\alpha^z_\Lambda(A).
$$
Moreover,
$$
\Lambda^c\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits\alpha^z_\Lambda(A)
\subset
\Lambda^c\cap(\Lambda\cup\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A)
=
\Lambda^c\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A.
$$
Applying  inequality~\eqref{mar-knee}  first with $K=\Lambda^c$ and then with
$K=\Lambda$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
\|\alpha^z_{-W_{\Lambda}(t)}(A)\|
&=\|\alpha^z_{\Lambda^c}\circ\alpha^z_\Lambda(A)\|\\
&\leq
\chi(\Lambda^c\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits\alpha^z_\Lambda(A))
\|\alpha_\Lambda^z(A)\|\\
&\leq
\chi(\Lambda^c\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A)
\chi(\Lambda\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A)\|A\|,
\end{align*}
as claimed.
\hfill$\Box$

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof combines formula~\eqref{eq:surf_energy_formula} for $W_\Lambda(t)$ and the
expansion~\eqref{eq:evol_chains}. The first term on the right-hand side of~\eqref{eq:surf_energy_formula} 
gives, using~\eqref{eq:need_chains4},
\begin{align*}
\sum_{X\subset\Lambda}(\tau^{-t}_\Phi-\tau^{-t}_{\Phi|_\Lambda})(\Psi(X))
&=\sum_{X\subset\Lambda}\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(-t)^n}{n!}\left(\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n(X)}D_\Phi(\boldsymbol{Y})\Psi(X)
-\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}^\Lambda_n(X)}D_\Phi(\boldsymbol{Y})\Psi(X)\right)\\[4pt]
&=\sum_{X\subset\Lambda }\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(-t)^n}{n!}\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n(X,\partial\Lambda)}
D_\Phi(\boldsymbol{Y})\Psi(X).
\end{align*}
For the second term, the same argument gives
$$
\sum_{X\subset\Lambda^c}(\tau^{-t}_\Phi-\tau^{-t}_{\Phi|_{\Lambda^c}})(\Psi(X))
=\sum_{X\subset\Lambda^c}\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(-t)^n}{n!}
\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n(X,\partial\Lambda)}
D_\Phi(\boldsymbol{Y})\Psi(X).
$$
For the third term, we use~\eqref{eq:surfacePsi} to obtain
$$
\tau^{-t}_\Phi(W_\Lambda(\Psi))=W_\Lambda(\Psi)+
\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{1}{X\cap\Lambda\neq\emptyset}{X\cap\Lambda^c\neq\emptyset}}
\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(-t)^n}{n!}
\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n(X,\partial\Lambda)}
D_\Phi(\boldsymbol{Y})\Psi(X).
$$
These three formulas add to
$$
W_\Lambda(t) =W_\Lambda(\Psi)+
\sum_{X\in{\mathcal F}}\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(-t)^n}{n!}\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n(X,\partial\Lambda)}
D_\Phi(\boldsymbol{Y})\Psi(X).
$$
We claim that this can be rewritten as~\eqref{eq:formula_Wt}. Indeed, let
$X\notin{\mathcal F}_\Lambda^\partial$ and
$\boldsymbol{Y}=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)\in{\mathcal C}_n(X,\partial\Lambda)$.
If $D_\Phi(\boldsymbol{Y})\Psi(X)\neq0$, then $\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits(Y_i)\le R$ for every
$i\in\llbracket1,n\rrbracket$; the chain property  gives
$\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(X,\partial\Lambda)\le nR$, and hence
$X\cap{\mathcal T}^\Lambda_n\neq\emptyset$.
\hfill$\Box$

label: lem:size_Tk
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:size_Tk}
There exists a constant $c>0$ such that, for every cube $\Lambda\in{\mathcal F}$
and every $n\geq1$, one has
$$
|{\mathcal T}^\Lambda_n|\leq c|\Lambda|^{1-1/d}n^d.

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We may assume that $\Lambda$ is centered at the origin.
If $2nR<|\Lambda|^{1/d}$, the set ${\mathcal T}_n^\Lambda$ lies in a
boundary layer of thickness $nR$ on either side of $\Lambda$.
Hence, for some constant $c_1>0$,
$$
|{\mathcal T}^\Lambda_n|\leq c_1|\Lambda|^{1-1/d}n^d.
$$
If $2nR\geq|\Lambda|^{1/d}$, then ${\mathcal T}^\Lambda_n$ is contained in a cube centered at the origin
of side at most $|\Lambda|^{1/d}+2nR\leq4nR$, and hence
$$
|{\mathcal T}^\Lambda_n|
\leq(4nR)^d
\leq c_2|\Lambda|^{1-1/d}n^d.
$$
Combining the two bounds yields the result.\hfill$\Box$

body_md:

For $K\subset{\mathbbm Z}^d$, $X\in{\mathcal F}$, $A\in{{\mathfrak{A}}_{\mathrm{loc}}}$, and $n\geq1$, one has
$$
\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n^K(X)}\prod_{i=1}^n\|\Psi(Y_i)\|\leq \mathrm{e}^{\rho|K\cap X|}\frac{n!}{(2\Theta_\Psi)^n},
$$
and
$$
\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal F}^n }\|D_{\Psi|_K}(\boldsymbol{Y})A\|\leq\mathrm{e}^{\rho|K\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A|}\frac{n!}{\Theta_\Psi^n}\|A\|.
$$

label: eq:Ruelle_est0
title: Proof
body_md:
Set $X=\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A$. By~\eqref{eq:need_chains3},
\begin{equation}
\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal F}^n}\|D_{\Psi|_K}(\boldsymbol{Y})A\|
=\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}^K_n(X)}\|D_\Psi(\boldsymbol{Y})A\|
\leq2^n\|A\|\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n^K(X)}
\prod_{i=1}^n\|\Psi(Y_i)\|.
\label{eq:Ruelle_est0}
\end{equation}
To bound the last sum, we follow~\cite[Eq.~(6.6)]{Ruelle1969}.
Let $\boldsymbol{Y}=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)\in{\mathcal C}_n^K(X)$, set $Q_1\coloneq X\cap K$ and, for 
$i\in\llbracket2,n\rrbracket$, $Q_i\coloneq(X\cap K)\cup\bigcup_{\ell=1}^{i-1}Y_\ell$.
Since $|Q_i|\leq|X\cap K|+\sum_{\ell=1}^{i-1}(|Y_\ell|-1)$, we have
$$
\sum_{Y_i\cap Q_i\neq\emptyset}\|\Psi(Y_i)\|\leq|Q_i|\sum_{Z_i\ni0}\|\Psi(Z_i)\|
\leq\left(|X\cap K|+\sum_{\ell=1}^{i-1}(|Y_\ell|-1)\right)\sum_{k_i\ge0}
\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{1}{Z_i\ni 0}{|Z_i|=k_i+1}}\|\Psi(Z_i)\|.
$$
Hence,
\begin{align*}
\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n^K(X)}\prod_{i=1}^n\|\Psi(Y_i)\|
&\leq
\sum_{Y_1\colon Y_1\cap Q_1\neq\emptyset}\cdots
\sum_{Y_n\colon Y_n\cap Q_n\neq\emptyset}
\prod_{i=1}^n\|\Psi(Y_i)\|\\
&\leq\sum_{(k_1,\ldots,k_n)\in{\mathbbm N}^n}\prod_{i=1}^n
\left((|X\cap K|+k_1+\ldots+k_{i-1})\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{1}{Z_i\ni0}{|Z_i|=k_i+1}}\|\Psi(Z_i)\|\right).
\end{align*}
The inequality
$$
\prod_{i=1}^n(|X\cap K|+k_1+\ldots+k_{i-1})\leq
(|X\cap K|+k_1+\ldots+k_n)^n
\le\mathrm{e}^{\rho|X \cap K|}\frac{n!}{\rho^n} \prod_{i=1}^n \mathrm{e}^{\rho k_i}
$$
gives
$$
\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n^K(X)}\prod_{i=1}^n\|\Psi(Y_i)\|
\leq\frac{n!}{\rho^n}\mathrm{e}^{\rho|X\cap K|}
\left(\sum_{Z\ni0}\mathrm{e}^{\rho(|Z|-1)}\|\Psi(Z)\|\right)^n
\leq n!\,\mathrm{e}^{\rho|X\cap K|}\left(\frac{\|\Psi\|_\rho}{\rho}\right)^n. 
$$
This proves the first bound. The second follows
from~\eqref{eq:Ruelle_est0}. \hfill$\Box$

label: prop:alphaK_exten
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:alphaK_exten} Fix $0<\theta<\Theta_\Psi$. Let
$\kappa_R\coloneq|\{x\in{\mathbbm Z}^d\mid |x|\leq R\}|$
be the number of lattice sites in the ball of radius $R$, and set
$$
T_\theta\coloneq
\mathrm{e}^{-\rho\kappa_R}\Theta_\Phi\left(1-\theta/\Theta_\Psi\right).
$$
Then, for all $K\subset{\mathbbm Z}^d$, $|t|<T_\theta$ and $A\in{{\mathfrak{A}}_{\mathrm{loc}}}$, the map 
$$
{\mathbbm R}\ni s\mapsto\alpha_K^s(A)\in{\mathfrak A}
$$
has an analytic extension to the strip $|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|<\theta$, and for any $z$ in this strip
$$
\|\alpha^z_K(A)\|\leq
\frac{\mathrm{e}^{(\rho+\eta)|\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A\cap K|}}
{\left(1-\theta/\Theta_\Psi\right)\left(1-|t|/T_\theta\right)}\|A\|.
$$
head: environment

label: eq:WG_bounds
title: Proof
body_md:
Set $C_{\Psi,\theta}=(1-\theta/\Theta_\Psi)^{-1}$. Let $A\in{{\mathfrak{A}}_{\mathrm{loc}}}$ and set $X=\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A$. 
For real $z$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:evol_chains} gives
$$
\tau^z_{\Psi|_K}\circ\tau^t_{\Phi|_K}(A)
=\tau^z_{\Psi|_K}(A)+\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{t^n}{n!}\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}^K_n(X)}\tau^z_{\Psi|_K}(D_\Phi(\boldsymbol{Y})A).
$$
For complex $z$ with $|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|<\theta$, we estimate the series on
the right-hand side. The bounds below will establish its locally
uniform convergence and justify the notation
$\tau^z_{\Psi|_K}\circ\tau^t_{\Phi|_K}(A)$.
After applying the isometry $\tau^{-t}_{\Phi|_K}$, we obtain
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
\|\alpha^z_K(A)\|=\|\tau^z_{\Psi|_K}\circ\tau^t_{\Phi|_K}(A)\|
&\le\|\tau^z_{\Psi|_K}(A)\|+\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{|t|^n}{n!}\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n^K(X)}\|\tau_{\Psi|_K}^z(D_\Phi(\boldsymbol{Y})A)\|\\ 
&\leq\left(1+\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(2|t|)^n}{n!}\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n^K(X)}
\prod_{i=1}^n\|\tau_{\Psi|_K}^z(\Phi(Y_i))\|\right)\| \tau_{\Psi|_K}^z(A)\|.
\end{split}
\label{eq:WG_bounds}
\end{equation}
Proposition~\ref{prop:ext_Ruelle} gives
$$
\|\tau^z_{\Psi|_K}(A)\|\leq C_{\Psi,\theta}\mathrm{e}^{\rho|K\cap X|}\|A\|,
$$
and 
$$
\|\tau^z_{\Psi|_K}(\Phi(Y))\|\leq C_{\Psi,\theta}\mathrm{e}^{\rho\kappa_R}\|\Phi(Y)\|
$$
for every $Y\in{\mathcal F}$. Moreover, Lemma~\ref{lem:Ruelle_chains}, applied to
$\Phi$ with the parameter $\eta$, gives
$$
\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n^K(X)}\prod_{i=1}^n\|\Phi(Y_i)\|
\le\mathrm{e}^{\eta|K\cap X|}\frac{n!}{(2\Theta_\Phi)^n}
$$
for every $n\ge1$. Substituting  these bounds into Eq.~\eqref{eq:WG_bounds}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
\|\alpha^z_K(A)\|
&\leq C_{\Psi,\theta}\mathrm{e}^{(\rho+\eta)|K\cap X|}\|A\|
\sum_{n\ge0}\left(\tfrac{2}{\eta}\|\Phi\|_\eta\mathrm{e}^{\rho\kappa_R}C_{\Psi,\theta}|t|\right)^n\\
&=\frac{\mathrm{e}^{(\rho+\eta)|K\cap X|}}
{1-(\theta/\Theta_\Psi+\mathrm{e}^{\rho\kappa_R}|t|/\Theta_\Phi)}\|A\|\\
&=\frac{\mathrm{e}^{(\rho+\eta)|K\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A|}}
{\left(1-\theta/\Theta_\Psi\right)\left(1-|t|/T_\theta\right)}\|A\|.         
\end{align*}
These bounds establish locally uniform convergence of the series
on $|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|<\theta$. Its sum agrees with
$\tau^z_{\Psi|_K}\circ\tau^t_{\Phi|_K}(A)$ for real $z$.
Applying $\tau^{-t}_{\Phi|_K}$ therefore gives the required analytic
extension of $\alpha_K^s(A)$, with the stated bound.
\hfill$\Box$

label: thm:alphaW_final
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:alphaW_final}
For any $0<\theta<\Theta_\Psi$ there exists $\overline T_\theta>0$ such that, for any $|t|<\overline T_\theta$ and
any cube $\Lambda\in{\mathcal F}$, the maps
$$
{\mathbbm R}\ni s\mapsto\alpha^s(W_\Lambda(t)),\qquad {\mathbbm R}\ni s\mapsto\alpha_{-W_{\Lambda}(t)}^s(W_\Lambda(t)),
$$ 
have analytic extensions to the strip $|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|<\theta$. Moreover, for $z$ in this strip,
$$
\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}\left(\|\alpha^{z}(W_\Lambda(t))\|+\|\alpha_{-W_{\Lambda}(t)}^z(W_\Lambda(t))\|\right)=0.
$$
head: environment

label: eq:salome
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $0<\theta<\Theta_\Psi$ and $0<\overline t<T_\theta$.
Suppose that $|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|<\theta$ and $|t|<\overline t$.
We first apply $\alpha^z$ termwise to the expansion in
Lemma~\ref{lem:WG_formula}, expanding $W_\Lambda(\Psi)$ into
its interaction terms. The estimates below establish locally
uniform convergence and justify denoting the resulting sum by
$\alpha^z(W_\Lambda(t))$. We obtain
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
&\|\alpha^z(W_\Lambda(t))\|
\le\|\alpha^z(W_\Lambda(\Psi))\|+\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\overline t^n}{n!}
\sum_{\substack{X\in{\mathcal F}\\
X\in{\mathcal F}_\Lambda^\partial\ \text{or}\ X\cap{\mathcal T}^\Lambda_n\neq\emptyset}}
\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n(X,\partial\Lambda)}\|\alpha^z(D_\Phi(\boldsymbol{Y})\Psi(X))\|\\
&\le\sum_{X\in{\mathcal F}_\Lambda^\partial}\|\alpha^z(\Psi(X))\|
+\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(2\overline t)^n}{n!}
\sum_{\substack{X\in{\mathcal F}\\
X\in{\mathcal F}_\Lambda^\partial\ \text{or}\ X\cap{\mathcal T}^\Lambda_n\neq\emptyset}}
\|\alpha^z(\Psi(X))\|\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n(X,\partial\Lambda)}
\prod_{i=1}^n\|\alpha^z(\Phi(Y_i))\|.
\end{split}
\label{eq:salome}
\end{equation}
For $X,Y\in{\mathcal F}$, Proposition~\ref{prop:alphaK_exten},
applied with $K={\mathbbm Z}^d$, gives
\begin{equation}
\|\alpha^z(\Psi(X))\|\leq\tilde C\mathrm{e}^{(\rho+\eta)|X|}\|\Psi(X)\|,\qquad 
\|\alpha^z(\Phi(Y))\|\leq\tilde C\mathrm{e}^{(\rho+\eta)\kappa_R}\|\Phi(Y)\|,
\label{eq:clouds}
\end{equation}
where $\tilde C\coloneq(1-\theta/\Theta_\Psi)^{-1}(1-\overline t/T_\theta)^{-1}$. 
Since $\rho+\eta<r$, \eqref{eq:clouds} gives
$$
\frac1{|\Lambda|}\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{1}{X\cap\Lambda\neq\emptyset}{X\cap\Lambda^c\neq\emptyset}}\|\alpha^z(\Psi(X))\|
\le\frac{\tilde C}{|\Lambda|}
\sum_{x\in\Lambda}\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{1}{X\ni0}{X\cap(\Lambda^c+x)\neq\emptyset}}
\mathrm{e}^{(\rho+\eta)|X|}\|\Psi(X)\|\rightarrow0,
$$
along centered cubes. The series over $n\geq1$ in~\eqref{eq:salome} is bounded by
$$
M_\Lambda\coloneq
\tilde C\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(2\tilde C\mathrm{e}^{(\rho+\eta)\kappa_R}\overline t)^n}{n!}
\sum_{\substack{X\in{\mathcal F}\\
X\in{\mathcal F}_\Lambda^\partial\ \text{or}\ X\cap{\mathcal T}^\Lambda_n\neq\emptyset}}
\mathrm{e}^{(\rho+\eta)|X|}\|\Psi(X)\|
\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n(X,\partial\Lambda)}\prod_{i=1}^n\|\Phi(Y_i)\|.
$$
Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:Ruelle_chains} to $\Phi$ with the parameter $\eta$, we get
$$
\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n(X,\partial\Lambda)}\prod_{i=1}^n\|\Phi(Y_i)\|
\le\mathrm{e}^{\eta|X|}\frac{n!}{(2\Theta_\Phi)^n}
$$
for every $X\in{\mathcal F}$ and $n\in{\mathbbm N}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:size_Tk} further gives  
$$
\sum_{X\cap{\mathcal T}_n^\Lambda\neq\emptyset}\mathrm{e}^{r_0|X|}\|\Psi(X)\|
\le\mathrm{e}^{r_0}\sum_{x\in{\mathcal T}_n^\Lambda}\sum_{X\ni x}\mathrm{e}^{r_0(|X|-1)}\|\Psi(X)\|
\leq c\mathrm{e}^{r_0}\|\Psi\|_{r_0}|\Lambda|^{1-1/d}n^d.
$$
Set
$$
b_\Lambda\coloneq
\frac1{|\Lambda|}\sum_{X\in{\mathcal F}_\Lambda^\partial}\mathrm{e}^{r_0|X|}\|\Psi(X)\|.
$$
Since $r_0<r$,
$$
b_\Lambda
\leq
\frac1{|\Lambda|}
\sum_{x\in\Lambda}
\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{1}{X\ni0}{X\cap(\Lambda^c+x)\neq\emptyset}}
\mathrm{e}^{r_0|X|}\|\Psi(X)\|
\rightarrow0
$$
along centered cubes. Consequently,
$$
\frac1{|\Lambda|}M_\Lambda\leq
\tilde C\sum_{n\ge1}
\left(\frac{\tilde C\mathrm{e}^{(\rho+\eta)\kappa_R}\overline t}{\Theta_\Phi}\right)^n
\left(c\mathrm{e}^{r_0}\|\Psi\|_{r_0}|\Lambda|^{-1/d}n^d+b_\Lambda\right)
\rightarrow0
$$
along centered cubes, provided that
$$
\overline t<T_1\coloneq\frac{T_\theta}{1+\mathrm{e}^{\eta\kappa_R}},
$$
which ensures convergence of the series.

For $\alpha_{-W_\Lambda(t)}$, the same argument gives
\begin{equation}
\|\alpha_{-W_{\Lambda}(t)}^z(W_\Lambda(t))\|
\le\sum_{X\in{\mathcal F}_\Lambda^\partial}
\|\alpha_{-W_{\Lambda}(t)}^z(\Psi(X))\|
+M_\Lambda',
\label{eq:rain}
\end{equation}
where
$$
M_\Lambda'=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(2\overline t)^n}{n!}
\sum_{\substack{X\in{\mathcal F}\\
X\in{\mathcal F}_\Lambda^\partial\ \text{or}\ X\cap{\mathcal T}^\Lambda_n\neq\emptyset}}
\|\alpha_{-W_{\Lambda}(t)}^z(\Psi(X))\|
\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_n(X,\partial\Lambda)}
\prod_{i=1}^n\|\alpha_{-W_{\Lambda}(t)}^z(\Phi(Y_i))\|.
$$
By Proposition~\ref{prop:alphaK_exten} and Lemma~\ref{lem:restricted_double_ineq}, the 
estimates~\eqref{eq:clouds} are replaced by
$$
\|\alpha^z_{-W_{\Lambda}(t)}(\Psi(X))\|
\leq\tilde C^2\mathrm{e}^{(\rho+\eta)|X|}\|\Psi(X)\|,\qquad
\|\alpha^z_{-W_{\Lambda}(t)}(\Phi(Y))\|
\leq\tilde C^2\mathrm{e}^{(\rho+\eta)\kappa_R}\|\Phi(Y)\|.
$$
Proceeding as above, the first term on the right-hand side of~\eqref{eq:rain} is
$o(|\Lambda|)$ along the centered cubes. For the second term, we get the estimate
$$
\frac1{|\Lambda|}M_\Lambda'\leq
\tilde C^2\sum_{n\ge1}
\left(\frac{\tilde C^2\mathrm{e}^{(\rho+\eta)\kappa_R}\overline t}{\Theta_\Phi}\right)^n
\left(c\mathrm{e}^{r_0}\|\Psi\|_{r_0}|\Lambda|^{-1/d}n^d+b_\Lambda\right)
\rightarrow0
$$
along the centered cubes, provided that the series converges. Since $\overline t<T_\theta/2$ implies
$$
\tilde C
\leq
\frac2{1-\theta/\Theta_\Psi},
$$
it is enough to require
$$
\overline t<T_2\coloneq
\min\left\{
\frac{T_\theta}{2},
\frac{\Theta_\Phi}{4}\mathrm{e}^{-(\rho+\eta)\kappa_R}
\left(1-\frac{\theta}{\Theta_\Psi}\right)^2
\right\}.
$$
The estimates also establish locally uniform convergence on
$|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|<\theta$ of both series obtained by termwise analytic
continuation. For real $z$, their sums agree with the corresponding
real-time evolutions of $W_\Lambda(t)$, and hence provide the
required analytic extensions. Thus, the assertions hold with
$\overline T_\theta\coloneq\min\{T_1,T_2\}$. \hfill$\Box$

label: lem:delta_Araki
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:delta_Araki}
For any $K\subset{\mathbbm Z}$ and $x\in{\mathbbm Z}$, one has
$$
\|\widehat{\Theta}_{K,x}\|
\leq
(L+1)\|\Theta\|_\mathrm{s}.
$$
Moreover, for every $A\in{{\mathfrak{A}}_{\mathrm{loc}}}$,
\begin{equation}
\delta_{\Theta|_K}(A)
=
\sum_{x\in{\mathbbm Z}}D_{\widehat{\Theta}_K}(x)A.
\label{eq:restricted_block_decomposition}
\end{equation}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The first assertion follows from
\[
\|\widehat{\Theta}_{K,x}\|
\leq
\sum_{\emptyset\neq X\subset{\mathbbm I}_L^x}\|\Theta(X)\|
\leq
\sum_{y\in{\mathbbm I}_L^x}\sum_{X\ni y}\|\Theta(X)\|
=
(L+1)\|\Theta\|_\mathrm{s}.
\]
Since every non-empty $X$ with $\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits(X)\leq L$ is contained in exactly
$N_L(X)$ intervals of the form ${\mathbbm I}_L^x$, we further have
\[
\sum_{x\in{\mathbbm Z}}D_{\widehat{\Theta}_K}(x)A
=
\sum_{x\in{\mathbbm Z}}
\sum_{\substack{\emptyset\neq X\subset K\cap{\mathbbm I}_L^x}}
\frac{\mathrm{i}[\Theta(X),A]}{N_L(X)}
=
\sum_{\substack{\emptyset\neq X\subset K\\X\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A\neq\emptyset}}
\mathrm{i}[\Theta(X),A]
=
\delta_{\Theta|_K}(A),
\]
which proves~\eqref{eq:restricted_block_decomposition}.
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: lem:HHhat
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{(i)} This follows from~\cite[Lemma~4.1 and the proof of Theorem~4.2]{Araki1969}.


\medskip\noindent\textbf{(ii)}
Iterating~\eqref{eq:restricted_block_decomposition} gives
$$
\delta_{\Theta|_K}^m(A)
=
\sum_{\boldsymbol{y}\in{\mathbbm Z}^m}D_{\widehat{\Theta}_K}(\boldsymbol{y})A.
$$
If a term in this sum does not vanish, then the support of
$\widehat{\Theta}_{K,y_1}$ intersects $K\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A\subset J$ and, successively,
the support of $\widehat{\Theta}_{K,y_j}$ intersects
$$
\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A\cup
\bigcup_{k=1}^{j-1}\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits\widehat{\Theta}_{K,y_k}.
$$
Since $\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits\widehat{\Theta}_{K,y_k}\subset{\mathbbm I}_L^{y_k}$, 
it follows that $\boldsymbol{y}\in{\mathcal C}'_{L,m}(J)$, which proves
\eqref{eq:restricted_block_iterates}.
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: prop:arakis_bound_dim1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:arakis_bound_dim1}
Let $\Theta\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$ have range $L$, and set
$$
C_\Theta\coloneq2(L+1)\|\Theta\|_\mathrm{s}.
$$
Let $K\subset{\mathbbm Z}$, $A\in{{\mathfrak{A}}_{\mathrm{loc}}}$, and let $n\geq L-1$ be such that
$K\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A$ is contained in an interval of length $n+1$. Then the map
$$
{\mathbbm R}\ni s\mapsto\tau_{\Theta|_K}^s(A)
$$
has an entire analytic extension and, for every $z\in{\mathbbm C}$,
\begin{equation}
\|\tau_{\Theta|_K}^z(A)\|
\leq
F_{L,n}(C_\Theta|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|)\|A\|.
\label{bound-knee}
\end{equation}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $J$ be an interval of length $n+1$ containing $K\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A$.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:HHhat},
\[
\|\delta_{\Theta|_K}^m(A)\|
\leq
\sum_{\boldsymbol{y}\in{\mathcal C}'_{L,m}(J)}
\|D_{\widehat{\Theta}_K}(\boldsymbol{y})A\|
\leq
2^m\|A\|
\sum_{\boldsymbol{y}\in{\mathcal C}'_{L,m}(J)}
\prod_{j=1}^m\|\widehat{\Theta}_{K,y_j}\|
\leq
C_\Theta^m|{\mathcal C}'_{L,m}(n)|\|A\|,
\]
where $|{\mathcal C}'_{L,m}(J)|=|{\mathcal C}'_{L,m}(n)|$ by translation. Hence, the Taylor series
$$
\sum_{m\geq0}\frac{z^m}{m!}\delta_{\Theta|_K}^m(A)
$$
converges in norm for every $z\in{\mathbbm C}$,  and
defines the entire analytic extension of $\tau_{\Theta|_K}^s(A)$. For
$z\in\mathrm{i}{\mathbbm R}$, Lemma~\ref{lem:HHhat}(i) gives
$$
\|\tau_{\Theta|_K}^z(A)\|
\leq
F_{L,n}(C_\Theta|z|)\|A\|.
$$
The bound~\eqref{bound-knee} follows from the group property and the isometry of the
real-time dynamics.
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: prop:arakis_bound
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:arakis_bound}
Let $t\in{\mathbbm R}$ and $K\subset{\mathbbm Z}$. Let $A\in{{\mathfrak{A}}_{\mathrm{loc}}}$, and let
$n\geq\max\{R-1,R'\}$ be such that $K\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A$ is contained in an
interval of length $n+1$. Then the map
$$
{\mathbbm R}\ni s\mapsto\alpha_K^s(A)
$$
has an entire analytic extension and, for every $z\in{\mathbbm C}$,
$$
\|\alpha_K^z(A)\|
\leq
G(t,|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|,n)\|A\|.
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose an interval $J$ of length $n+1$ containing $K\cap\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits A$.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:HHhat},
$$
\tau_{\Phi|_K}^t(A)
=
\sum_{m\geq0}\frac{t^m}{m!}
\sum_{\boldsymbol{y}\in{\mathcal C}'_{R',m}(J)}
D_{\widehat{\Phi}_K}(\boldsymbol{y})A.
$$
For real $s$, we apply $\tau_{\Psi|_K}^s$ termwise and then
$\tau_{\Phi|_K}^{-t}$. The estimates below show that the resulting
series, with $s$ replaced by $z$, converges locally uniformly on ${\mathbbm C}$
and defines the entire extension $\alpha_K^z(A)$.


Set
$$
f(z)\coloneq F_{R,n}(C_\Psi|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|).
$$
Proposition~\ref{prop:arakis_bound_dim1} gives
$$
\|\tau_{\Psi|_K}^z(A)\|
\leq
f(z)\|A\|,
\qquad
\|\tau_{\Psi|_K}^z(\widehat{\Phi}_{K,y})\|
\leq
\frac{C_\Phi}{2}f(z).
$$
These bounds yield
\[
\left\|
\tau_{\Psi|_K}^z
\left(
D_{\widehat{\Phi}_K}(\boldsymbol{y})A
\right)
\right\|\leq
2^m
\|\tau_{\Psi|_K}^z(A)\|
\prod_{j=1}^m
\|\tau_{\Psi|_K}^z(\widehat{\Phi}_{K,y_j})\|\leq
C_\Phi^m f(z)^{m+1}\|A\|.
\]
Since $\tau_{\Phi|_K}^{-t}$ is isometric, it follows that
\begin{align*}
\|\alpha_K^z(A)\|
&\leq
f(z)
\sum_{m\geq0}
\frac{\left(C_\Phi|t|f(z)\right)^m}{m!}
|{\mathcal C}'_{R',m}(n)|\,\|A\|\\
&=
F_{R,n}(C_\Psi|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|)
F_{R',n}
\left(
C_\Phi|t|F_{R,n}(C_\Psi|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|)
\right)\|A\|,
\end{align*}
as claimed.
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

title: Remark
body_md: For fixed $t\in{\mathbbm R}$ and $u\geq0$, the function $n\mapsto G(t,u,n)$ is non-decreasing.
head: environment

label: thm:d1_extension
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:d1_extension}
Let $t\in{\mathbbm R}$. For any interval
$\Lambda=\llbracket a,b\rrbracket\subset{\mathbbm Z}$, the maps
$$
{\mathbbm R}\ni s\mapsto\alpha^s(W_\Lambda(t)),
\qquad
{\mathbbm R}\ni s\mapsto
\alpha^s_{-W_\Lambda(t)}(W_\Lambda(t))
$$
have entire analytic extensions. Moreover, for every $a_0>0$ there exists a
constant $C_{t,a_0}$, independent of $\Lambda$, such that
$$
\sup_{|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|<a_0}
\left(
\|\alpha^z(W_\Lambda(t))\|
+
\|\alpha^z_{-W_\Lambda(t)}(W_\Lambda(t))\|
\right)
\leq
C_{t,a_0}.
$$
head: environment

label: eq:Q_block_expansion
title: Proof
body_md:
Set $n_0\coloneq\max\{R,R'\}$. 
For $X\in{\mathcal F}$, $K\subset{\mathbbm Z}$, and $m\geq0$, define
$$
Q_K^{(m)}(X)
\coloneq
\delta_{\Phi|_K}^m(\Psi(X))
=
\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_m^K(X)}D_\Phi(\boldsymbol{Y})\Psi(X).
$$
If $\Psi(X)\neq0$, choose an interval $J_X$ of length $n_0+1$ containing
$X$. Lemma~\ref{lem:HHhat} gives
\begin{equation}
Q_K^{(m)}(X)
=
\sum_{\boldsymbol{y}\in{\mathcal C}'_{R',m}(J_X)}
D_{\widehat{\Phi}_K}(\boldsymbol{y})\Psi(X).
\label{eq:Q_block_expansion}
\end{equation}
For an interval $\Lambda\subset{\mathbbm Z}$, set
$$
B_\Lambda^{(m)}(X)
\coloneq
\sum_{\boldsymbol{Y}\in{\mathcal C}_m(X,\partial\Lambda)}
D_\Phi(\boldsymbol{Y})\Psi(X).
$$
By~\eqref{eq:need_chains4},
\begin{equation}
B_\Lambda^{(m)}(X)
=
\begin{cases}
Q_{\mathbbm Z}^{(m)}(X)-Q_\Lambda^{(m)}(X)
&\text{if }X\subset\Lambda;\\[4pt]
Q_{\mathbbm Z}^{(m)}(X)-Q_{\Lambda^c}^{(m)}(X)
&\text{if }X\subset\Lambda^c;\\[4pt]
Q_{\mathbbm Z}^{(m)}(X)
&\text{if }X\cap\Lambda\neq\emptyset\neq X\cap\Lambda^c.
\end{cases}
\label{eq:boundary_Q_decomposition}
\end{equation}
For $|t|<\Theta_\Phi$, Lemma~\ref{lem:WG_formula} and
\eqref{eq:boundary_Q_decomposition} give
\begin{equation}
W_\Lambda(t)
=
\sum_{m\geq0}\frac{(-t)^m}{m!}
\sum_{X\in{\mathcal F}}B_\Lambda^{(m)}(X).
\label{eq:formula_Wt_1d}
\end{equation}
We proceed to  show that the series on the right-hand side converges
locally uniformly in $t\in{\mathbbm C}$ and hence defines an entire ${\mathfrak A}$-valued
function.

If $B_\Lambda^{(m)}(X)\neq0$ and $\Psi(X)\neq0$, then
$$
X\cap{\mathcal T}_m^\Lambda\neq\emptyset,
\qquad
{\mathcal T}_m^\Lambda
\coloneq
\left\{
x\in{\mathbbm Z}\mid
\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(\{x\},\partial\Lambda)\leq R+mR'
\right\}.
$$
There exists a constant $c>0$, independent of $\Lambda$ and $m$, such that
\begin{equation}
|{\mathcal T}_m^\Lambda|
\leq
c(1+m).
\label{eq:one_dim_tube_bound}
\end{equation}
Moreover, Lemma~\ref{lem:delta_Araki} and
\eqref{eq:Q_block_expansion} give
$$
\|Q_K^{(m)}(X)\|
\leq
C_\Phi^m
|{\mathcal C}'_{R',m}(n_0)|
\|\Psi(X)\|,
$$
and hence
$$
\|B_\Lambda^{(m)}(X)\|
\leq
2C_\Phi^m
|{\mathcal C}'_{R',m}(n_0)|
\|\Psi(X)\|.
$$
It follows that
\begin{equation}
\sum_{m\geq0}\frac{|t|^m}{m!}
\sum_{X\in{\mathcal F}}\|B_\Lambda^{(m)}(X)\|
\leq
2c\|\Psi\|_\mathrm{s}
\sum_{m\geq0}
(1+m)
\frac{(C_\Phi|t|)^m}{m!}
|{\mathcal C}'_{R',m}(n_0)|
<\infty,
\label{mar-phy-bb}
\end{equation}
where the last assertion follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:HHhat}(i). The same estimates apply to the Taylor series of
$W_{\Lambda,\widetilde\Lambda}(t)$, uniformly in
$\widetilde\Lambda\supset\Lambda$. Since the interactions have finite
range, each coefficient agrees with the corresponding coefficient
in~\eqref{eq:formula_Wt_1d} once $\widetilde\Lambda$ is sufficiently
large. The  bound~\eqref{mar-phy-bb} gives locally uniform convergence on
${\mathbbm C}$ to the right-hand side of~\eqref{eq:formula_Wt_1d}.
For real $t$, Proposition~\ref{prop:formula_W} identifies this limit
with $W_\Lambda(t)$. Thus~\eqref{eq:formula_Wt_1d} holds for every
$t\in{\mathbbm R}$ and defines an entire ${\mathfrak A}$-valued extension of
$t\mapsto W_\Lambda(t)$.




Fix $a_0>0$ and set $g\coloneq G(t,a_0,n_0)$. 
For $|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|<a_0$, Proposition~\ref{prop:arakis_bound} and
\eqref{eq:Q_block_expansion} give
\begin{equation}
\|\alpha^z(Q_K^{(m)}(X))\|
\leq
C_\Phi^m
|{\mathcal C}'_{R',m}(n_0)|
g^{m+1}
\|\Psi(X)\|,
\label{eq:Q_alpha_bound}
\end{equation}
uniformly in $K\subset{\mathbbm Z}$. Combining
\eqref{eq:formula_Wt_1d},
\eqref{eq:boundary_Q_decomposition},
\eqref{eq:one_dim_tube_bound}, and
\eqref{eq:Q_alpha_bound}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
\|\alpha^z(W_\Lambda(t))\|
&\leq
2cg\|\Psi\|_\mathrm{s}
\sum_{m\geq0}
(1+m)
\frac{(C_\Phi g|t|)^m}{m!}
|{\mathcal C}'_{R',m}(n_0)|.
\end{align*}
The bound is finite and uniform in $\Lambda$ and $|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|<a_0$.
Since $a_0>0$ is arbitrary, the series
$$
\alpha^z(W_\Lambda(t))
=
\sum_{m\geq0}\frac{(-t)^m}{m!}
\sum_{X\in{\mathcal F}}\alpha^z(B_\Lambda^{(m)}(X))
$$
converges locally uniformly on ${\mathbbm C}$ and provides the required entire
extension.

For a non-empty finite set $Y\subset{\mathbbm Z}$, set
$$
n(Y)\coloneq\max\{\mathop{\oslash}\nolimits(Y),R-1,R'\},
\qquad
\chi_{a_0}(Y)\coloneq G(t,a_0,n(Y)),\qquad \chi_{a_0}(\emptyset)=1.
$$
By the preceding remark,
$\chi_{a_0}$ is non-decreasing. Proposition~\ref{prop:arakis_bound}
therefore verifies the assumptions of
Lemma~\ref{lem:restricted_double_ineq} on the strip
$|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|<a_0$. In particular,
$$
\|\alpha^z_{-W_\Lambda(t)}(\Psi(X))\|
\leq
g^2\|\Psi(X)\|,
\qquad
\|\alpha^z_{-W_\Lambda(t)}(\widehat{\Phi}_{K,y})\|
\leq
\frac{C_\Phi}{2}g^2.
$$
Using again
\eqref{eq:Q_block_expansion}, we obtain
$$
\|\alpha^z_{-W_\Lambda(t)}(Q_K^{(m)}(X))\|
\leq
C_\Phi^m
|{\mathcal C}'_{R',m}(n_0)|
g^{2m+2}
\|\Psi(X)\|,
$$
uniformly in $K$ and $\Lambda$. Consequently,
\begin{align*}
\|\alpha^z_{-W_\Lambda(t)}(W_\Lambda(t))\|
&\leq
2cg^2\|\Psi\|_\mathrm{s}
\sum_{m\geq0}
(1+m)
\frac{(C_\Phi g^2|t|)^m}{m!}
|{\mathcal C}'_{R',m}(n_0)|.
\end{align*}
The estimate shows that applying $\alpha_{-W_\Lambda(t)}^z$
termwise to~\eqref{eq:formula_Wt_1d} gives an operator series
converging uniformly for $|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|<a_0$, with its sum bounded
independently of $\Lambda$. For real $z=s$, this sum equals
$\alpha_{-W_\Lambda(t)}^s(W_\Lambda(t))$. Since $a_0>0$ is
arbitrary, the series provides  the required entire extension.
\hfill$\Box$
